hints: A query selects the original coins at positions a through b; their order does not matter for subset sums.
Sort only the values in that selected range and maintain the largest continuously reachable sum x.
A coin c<=x+1 extends reachable sums through x+c; the first larger coin exposes the missing x+1.
analogy: Within each selected bag of coins, grow the covered sum interval until the next coin is too large to bridge its next gap.
algorithm: Build a persistent segment tree over coin values for each array prefix, storing counts and value sums. For query [a,b], use roots b and a-1 to obtain count/sum of values <=T. Start T=0; query the sum S of selected coins <=T+1; if S=T stop and answer T+1, otherwise set T=S and repeat. Use coordinate compression and wide sums.
correctness: The persistent-root difference represents exactly the coins in index range [a,b]. At each step all coins <=T+1 extend the reachable interval, whose new endpoint is their total sum; when that sum no longer changes, the next value T+1 cannot be formed.
complexity: O(n log n) preprocessing and memory; each query uses O(log n) per threshold iteration, with O(log n) iterations because T at least doubles when it grows.
example: For query positions 2..4 in [2,9,1,2,7], the selected coins are 9,1,2. Sorted 1,2,9 cover sums 1,2,3, so the smallest missing sum is 4.
